To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The long-run properties of a model can be estimated using a transformed regression model that omits the short-run dynamics.

(a) the long run can be estimated by OLS on a transformed model, (b) the long run is unaffected by short-run dynamics if the regressors that enter the long run are trend-stationar, and (c) if the long run is of interest, the dynamic model that is best specified is one that has the same regressors in the long-run and short-run equations, and in which the long-run equation is the only one that contains a constant

If the variables that enter the cointegrating relation are trend-station-ary then the long-run multipliers can be estimated without any short-run dynamics and without the need to impose the long-run restrictions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the specification, estimation, and testing of dynamic econometric models.
the specification, estimation, and testing of dynamic economic models, with particular emphasis on the long run and the estimation of transformed regression models.
the estimation of dynamic econometric models in which the focus of interest is the long-run properties of the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dynamic econometric models are best formulated as transformed regression models.

, if the long-run solution is of interest, the most efficient way to formulate and to estimate the dynamic model is to use a transformed regression model in which the long-run solution can be estimated directly and in which the short-run dynamic specification is not critical to the estimation of the long-run parameters.
the long-run coefficients are best estimated by regressing the transformed data on a constant and the long-run explanatory variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to provide the long-run multipliers for any dynamic model, even in the presence of serial correlation.
dynamic econometric models can be formulated and estimated in a variety of ways.
we show how to obtain the long run properties of a model from a dynamic specification, and how to estimate them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the long run is not a separate entity, but a part of the dynamic system.
the dynamic structure of a model is not as important as is commonly supposed.
, in the context of dynamic models, there is a clear distinction to be drawn between the short-run and the long-run.
